intro.title: Build blue green deploy readiness endpoint set
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a set of readiness endpoints for a blue-green deployment system using Node.js. You will create a simple Express server with two separate endpoints: one for the 'blue' environment and one for the 'green' environment, each returning a status to indicate if it is ready to serve traffic. The core programming concept involves setting up HTTP servers, defining route handlers, and managing basic application state to simulate deployment readiness. You will use key Node.js technologies like the Express framework and the built-in HTTP module to handle web requests. By the end, you will understand how to implement and test readiness checks that are essential for safe, zero-downtime deployments.
intro.usecase: Blue-green deployment readiness endpoints are critical in production systems where zero-downtime updates are required, such as e-commerce platforms during holiday sales or banking applications processing transactions 24/7. Developers implement these health-check endpoints in deployment dashboards and CI/CD pipelines to validate that new versions can safely handle live traffic before switching over. For example, a streaming service like Netflix uses readiness probes to ensure new recommendation algorithms work correctly before directing users to updated servers, preventing service disruptions during global releases.

objectives: Construct a basic Express server with two separate endpoints for blue and green deployments
Configure environment variables to control which deployment version is currently active
Implement a readiness check endpoint that returns the status of the active deployment
Initialize a version tracking system to distinguish between blue and green deployments
Apply conditional logic to route traffic based on deployment status
Manipulate response headers to indicate deployment version in API responses
Integrate a simple health monitoring mechanism for both deployment environments
